Criterion: Verify that the control system maintains both stable engine operation and response during all steady state and transient conditions. Standard: All engine control loops demonstrate a minimum of 6 db gain margin and 45 degrees of phase margin. The engine provides safe and stable thrust/power levels in response to all operator commands. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, and review of documentation. Phase and gain stability margins are verified through analysis, open and closed loop modeling, bench testing (wet rig) and full-up engine testing. These verification methods are conducted using the entire range of expected power level angle inputs and transients. Closed loop models are validated using closed loop bench and full-up engine testing. Ground and flight testing demonstrate the engine's ability to respond to all pilot/operator commands. References: JSSG-2007: A.3.7.2, A.4.7.2 Control systems guidance MIL-HDBK-516: 7.2.2.2. 14 CFR 33.27, 33.28, 33.91

Standard: Control system maintains both stable engine operation and response during all steady state and transient operations. Engine control loops maintain a minimum of 6 dB gain margin and 45 degrees of phase margin. The engine provides stable thrust and power levels in response to flight crew commands using the entire range of power setting inputs and transients. For turboshaft applications, the engine control system stability has gain and phase margin to prevent dynamic coupling with the rotor system or propeller during steady state and transient operation. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review documentation (e.g., ICD, design data records, and other substantiating records and reports) and verify that the design meets phase and gain stability margins. Analysis.
  (1) Design analysis verifies phase and gain stability margins. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Closed loop bench tests verify phase and gain stability margins.
    (2) Lab test: Ground-based sea level cell tests verify the engine phase and gain stability margins. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (3) Flight test: Flight testing verifies the engine's ability to respond to flight crew commands.
